content.title: What If Tonight Is Your Last Night?
content.subtitle: From a soft bed to three and a half cubits of earth.
content.body:
When we suddenly wake up thirsty at night, our hand instinctively reaches for the glass of water beside the bed. When a cool breeze touches us, we pull the blanket closer. Sometimes we leave a dim night light on, fearing the darkness if we wake suddenly. But imagine: what if tonight is your last night in this world? There will be no soft pillow beneath your head, only hard earth. Instead of your familiar ceiling, an impenetrable darkness of three and a half cubits of damp earth will surround you.

Where There Is No Switch to Turn On the Light

There will be no switchboard to reach for when darkness overwhelms you, no phone to send a desperate message: “I feel suffocated. I am terribly afraid. Please, someone, come and just talk to me.”

The spouse whose embrace made you forget life's weariness, the child whose slightest cough kept you awake, neither will descend into the earth to share your loneliness. Your worldly power, expensive perfume, career, and social pride will remain above the ground. On that motionless bed in the grave, your companions will be the damp smell of earth and heartbreaking silence.

The Heartbreaking Plea to Return

When the solemn moment of questioning draws near, neither worldly power nor bank balance will protect you. You will only wish: If only I could return one more time!

Allah reminds us of this desperate plea in the Qur’an:

“Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, ‘My Lord, send me back, so that I may do righteousness in what I left behind."

(Surah Al-Mu’minun: 99–100)

But alas, the road back will be closed forever. In that absolute darkness beneath the earth, when worldly relationships have turned to dust, only one companion will remain: your deeds.

The secret charity no one knew about- easing a broken heart, or tears shed in the stillness of night out of fear of your Lord, perhaps these will become a gentle light in your grave. But if there is neglect, arrogance, and hidden sin, that darkness may become like a poisonous serpent, silently tightening its grip.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“Indeed, the grave is the first stage of the Hereafter. Whoever is saved from it, what comes after will be easier. And whoever is not saved from it, what comes after will be harder.”

(Tirmidhi: 2308)

Return Before It Is Too Late

Tonight, you may lie down on your soft bed, pull the blanket over yourself, and close your eyes peacefully. But who knows? Perhaps the decree has already been written that tomorrow night will not be spent on this soft bed, but in the cold embrace of three and a half cubits of earth.

None of us knows how long the soul will remain within this golden cage called the body. So, while breath still moves through your chest, while you can still shed tears of remorse and raise your hands to your Lord, return to Him.

Before the walls of earth close around you, fall into a private prostration and ask Him to wash away the sins of a lifetime. What better time could there be than this silent night?

Come, let us return to Him before He calls us back!
